title: When a Torus Family Becomes S6
hook: Does S^6 admit a complex structure? Yup.
single_move: smooth torus family degenerates at the cusp into a hexagonal dP6 toric fibre
source_facts: three special points: elliptic order 3, elliptic order 4, cusp
cusp monodromy is unipotent of rank two
central toric fibre W has a hexagonal moment polygon and is a self-glued degree-six del Pezzo dP6
pi_1(X)=Z/|12 ell_0 - 4 ell_1 - 3 ell_2| and the chosen parameters give 1
integral homology of X is that of S6 and X is diffeomorphic to S6
Euler number localises at the cusp: e(X)=e(W)=2
visual_beats: one smooth torus repeats over a dark base curve
cusp monodromy twists the fibre and opens a seam
the torus collapses into a six-sided hexagonal dP6 surface
the seam closes and the total space resolves to S6
falsifier: If the rendered transition does not preserve the three special points, cusp monodromy, hexagon/dP6 fibre and S6 closure, reject the film.
